issue.title: Independent implement phases (slice scheduler + stacked PRs + forest constraint)

summary: Architecture analysis for splitting the monolithic implement phase into a DAG of independent slices. Each slice runs on its own branch with a fresh agent team and per-slice BRC consensus, then opens its own PR stacked along the DAG. Renames Phase→Slice in the contract; introduces forest-constraint validation at plan ingestion; namespaces the BRC tracker with nested pipeline IDs for slice consensus while keeping pipeline-level cross-cutting messages (HEARTBEAT, OVERSEER_ALERT) flat; reuses ExecutionWave/compute_waves for scheduling; per-slice branch via create_phase_worktree (already in gateway, never wired into runtime); GitHub auto-retarget plus a periodic reconciler for stacked-PR rebase mechanics. Single-PR delivery for #2137 itself (≈1,500–2,500 LOC across orchestrator/, gateway/, shared/egg_contracts/, plus prompts/docs).

problem_statement.description: The implement phase today is monolithic: one branch (egg/issue-N), one agent team spawned in a single concurrent wave, one BRC consensus round across the entire feature diff, and one PR per ticket. Tickets large enough to fill the context window cause compaction and a measurable drop in output quality. Closed PR #2152 (issue #2139) already tore out reviewer_code subagent fan-out and promoted reviewer_security/reviewer_concurrency to CRITICAL, deliberately leaving #2137 as the producer-side fix.
goals: Split implement into a DAG of independent slices, each scoped small enough that a single agent can implement it (≲1,000 LOC, advisory).
Schedule slices into parallel waves via ExecutionWave; independent slices run concurrently with no orchestrator-imposed concurrency cap.
Each slice runs on its own branch with a fresh agent team and a per-slice BRC consensus round using the full implement-phase reviewer roster.
Each slice opens its own PR. Root slices target the pipeline branch; single-parent slices target their parent slice's branch (stacked).
Lift the one-PR-per-pipeline constraint (load-bearing for #1557's epic pipeline).
non_goals: Multi-parent slices (diamond DAGs) — MVP enforces a forest constraint; planner auto-serializes would-be multi-parent slices into chains.
Cross-slice architectural review pass — lens reviewers (reviewer_security, reviewer_concurrency, reviewer_code_holistic) run per-slice only.
Refine and plan phase orchestration — unchanged; they remain monolithic.
babysit_pr pipelines — unchanged (#2063 stays separate; follow-up tracked).
Per-slice MCP control verbs — #2137 exposes the internal slice-addressable hooks; the verb layer (restart_slice, get_slice_status, list_slices) lands in #2199 immediately after.
Reviewer roster cleanup and lens promotion — already landed in #2152.

components.name: Slice scheduler (orchestrator run-loop integration)
components.responsibility: Replace the implement phase's single-wave dispatch with a wave-driven loop: build a slice-keyed DependencyGraph from contract.slices[], call compute_waves(), and for each wave spawn one slice in parallel up to DAG width (no concurrency cap). Each slice's lifecycle: provision branch (C5) → spawn agent team via ConcurrentPhaseExecutor-equivalent (C4) → await per-slice BRC CONFIRMED (C6) → open per-slice PR (C7) → mark slice complete in contract → advance.

data_flow: 1. Refine phase emits .egg-state/drafts/2137-analysis.md (already done; this output is plan-phase work).
2. Plan phase emits .egg-state/drafts/2137-plan.md with slices[] (each slice has id, name, status, max_cycles, tasks[], dependencies[], optional serialized_chain_order).
3. Orchestrator's _populate_contract_from_plan populates Contract.slices[] AND validates the forest constraint; non-forest plans hit a structured error that surfaces to reviewer_plan as a NACK.
4. Implement phase enters; the slice loop builds a slice-keyed DependencyGraph and calls compute_waves(). Wave 0 = root slices (no dependencies).

5. For each slice in the wave, the orchestrator: provisions egg/issue-2137/slice-M via create_phase_worktree (base = pipeline branch for root, parent slice's branch for child); registers a tracker on issue-2137/slice-M; spawns the full implement roster.
6. Per-slice BRC runs: producers PROPOSE → reviewers ACK/NACK → CONFIRMED. Slice-local max_cycles=3; pipeline-wide max_cycles=10 (two-tier per decision-9).
7. On CONFIRMED, the orchestrator opens a per-slice PR (root → pipeline branch; child → parent slice's branch). Slice marked complete in contract.

8. Wave advances: dependent slices spawn once their parent CONFIRMS. Failure path: slice failure → HITL decision; 60s grace; if unresolved, walk DAG and abort downstream + OVERSEER_ALERT (decision-10).
9. Reconciler runs in the background: periodically polls slice PRs; force-push or out-of-band base deletion → explicit rebase via gateway (decision-16).

10. Once all slices CONFIRM and PRs are open, the implement phase advances to PR phase — PR phase scope is unchanged (still emits one phase-level summary PR? or terminates? — plan-phase needs to confirm with task_planner / risk_analyst whether PR phase is even required when implement already created N PRs).

operational_notes_from_feedback: feedback-1 Q1 — typical 3–7 slices; worst-case 10–15; default max_parallel_slices = 5 reasonable starting point if/when an operational cap is added (not part of #2137 since decision-5 = unbounded).

feedback-1 Q2 — single PR delivery for #2137 itself; splitting #2137 into multiple PRs presupposes the multi-PR feature it introduces. Scope: 1,500–2,500 LOC across orchestrator/, gateway/, shared/egg_contracts/, plan_parser/, agent prompts.
feedback-1 Q3 — branch convention is egg/issue-N/slice-M (slash-separated; matches egg/babysit-pr/{pr}/{sha}/{role} precedent and gh-stack guidance).

feedback-1 Q4 — no specific known caps today; trust gateway / container / GHA queue throttling. #2199 follow-up: per-slice MCP control verbs (restart_slice, get_slice_status, list_slices). #2137 must expose internal slice-addressable hooks so #2199 can wrap them.
feedback-1 Q5 — nothing to salvage from reviewer_code fan-out; #2152 was a clean tear-out.
feedback-1 Q6 — leave regression-benchmark ticket choice to implement phase or operator; any ticket >33K LOC / 41 files works.
risk_summary_for_risk_analyst: Cross-slice architectural defects invisible to per-slice CRITICAL reviewers (reviewer_code_holistic only sees one slice). Explicitly accepted MVP risk per recommendation caveat 4.
Forest constraint may force unnatural serializations that slow the pipeline (5-slice DAG with two diamonds collapses to a chain of 3+2; latency reverts toward monolithic).
Stacked-PR rebase on parent merge is a known sharp edge in GitHub: auto-retarget is reliable only via UI/gh pr merge, not force-push. Reconciler mitigates but adds complexity.
BRC tracker namespacing is net-new; concurrent slice consensus on the same pipeline must not cross-talk (every existing tracker call site must be audited for tracker_id discipline).
Two-tier max_cycles introduces a new pipeline-wide budget counter; off-by-one in counter increments could exhaust the budget prematurely or never trip the cap.
60s grace period before downstream-DAG abort is a tunable; too tight → spurious abort while a human is reading the HITL; too loose → idle slices burn slots while waiting.

Slicing applies to ALL implement phases, including small tickets that wouldn't compact. Small tickets pay the slice overhead (per-slice tracker, per-slice PR, per-slice CI) without benefit. Not a #2137 acceptance criterion to gate slicing on complexity, but worth flagging.

Schema rename has wide reach (Pydantic model + parser + plan template + docs + agent prompts). Migration validator must be tested against any in-flight contracts persisted under the legacy phases[] shape.
DependencyGraph generification risks behavioral drift for the role-keyed callers if not type-narrowed cleanly.
Cost / token multiplier: 5-slice ticket with full roster per slice ≈ 5× today's agent count; per-PR CI also multiplies. No cap is enforced (decision-5).
Per-slice MCP verbs (#2199) depend on internal hooks #2137 exposes; if hooks are not slice-id-parameterized the follow-up will need refactoring rather than wrapping.
